g.textArea: BIC Claim Assistant · 29 October 2026 · Decide ADR003–ADR007 and the release team agreements

🎯 Goal
Move 5 proposed ADRs to accepted or rejected, and agree how we work around a release.
Before the meeting (10 min)
Read "Release candidates explained" on the wiki and put your concerns as orange stickies in 💬 CONCERNS on each ADR frame.
Agenda (30 min)
0:00 · Why we are here (frames 0–1) · 3 min
0:03 · ADR003 How do we release? · 6 min
0:09 · ADR004 Tags, changelog, release notes · 4 min
0:13 · ADR005 Preview environment · 4 min
0:17 · ADR006 Hotfix process · 4 min
0:21 · ADR007 Rollback · 4 min
0:25 · Team agreements · 3 min
0:28 · Results, owners, next steps · 2 min

🗳 How we vote (per ADR, 4 min)
0. Before the meeting: orange stickies in 💬 CONCERNS
1. 1 min: the owner recaps the proposal
2. 2 min: discuss the concerns
3. 1 min: vote with Miro Voting – 1 vote per decider
✅ Accept 🟡 Accept with action points ❌ Reject
4. Passed = most deciders accept (✅ + 🟡) and nobody has a blocking reason. Blocking reasons are written down.
ADR003 gets 6 min: it has an extra sub-vote.
An accepted ADR does not change anymore; a new ADR supersedes it.
Out of time? Result becomes 🟡 with action points. We move on.

g.text: Deciders: BIC team – Engineers and PO

rect.data-content: Ricardo Mayerhofer
Ricardo Campo
Advisor: QA

23 of 39
pipeline runs from main timed out at the ACC approval (mid-June – 15 Oct 2026).
Their changes only reached PRD if a later run rebuilt the same apps.

31 of 72
CD runs deployed a feature branch into the shared TST.
A fix/ branch reached ACC. A deploy/ branch reached PRD – its commit never reached main.

0 release tags
No changelog, no release notes.
k8s-deployments records the wrong commit: nobody can say quickly what runs in PRD.

No agreed hotfix or rollback process
Approving an older run silently deploys older images.
The ArgoCD rollback button does not stick.
Preview environment for feature branches (TST stays = main)
Pull request
Release candidate (RC)
RC = the version of every app + CDK stacks + WSO2 config, built from one commit of main. Build once, promote everywhere.
Tag release/YYYY.MM.DD + changelog + release notes

g.textArea:
Today we decide 5 things:
ADR003 How we release · ADR004 How we mark releases
ADR005 Where we test branches · ADR006 Hotfixes · ADR007 Rollback

g.text: ADR003 · Promote release candidates to PRD
g.textArea: How do we release – so nothing merged is missed, nothing goes back by accident, and we know what is in PRD?

rect.data-content:
A. Keep the current process
Approve the right runs, re-run what was missed.
✗ Changes still missed ✗ Old approvals can roll PRD back

B. Since the last release tag
Tag every PRD release; CI builds everything changed since that tag (Score team does this).
✓ Small, proven ✗ Old approvals can still deploy older images ✗ Rollback = rebuild

⭐ C. Release candidates
Every merge to main publishes an RC: version of every app + CDK + WSO2. Promote TST → ACC → PRD.
✓ Meets all 5 decision drivers

D. Release branches
✗ Branch overhead and merge-back mistakes
✗ Conflicts with trunk-based development and NX affected

E. Always build and deploy everything
✗ Every release restarts every app
✗ PRD gets images ACC did not test

F. A pipeline per app
✗ 5 apps × 3 environments = 15 approvals
✗ Portal + BFF and ingestion + CDK need manual coordination

tr.td: Same image in ACC and PRD

g.textArea:
Proposal: C. Release candidates
• An RC = the version of every app + CDK stacks + WSO2 config, from one commit of main
• CD compares the RC with the environment and only updates what differs
• A guard refuses an older RC, unless it is a deliberate rollback (ROLLBACK=true)
• Build once: the image tested in ACC is the image in PRD
• Rollback = promote the previous RC (see ADR007)
• Interim if we want the smallest first step: B (its release tag step is reused by C)
📏 Rule that comes with it:
Only merge to main what may go to PRD with the next release.
Unfinished work stays in its PR (show it in the preview environment).

rect.data-content: Pipeline work: RC manifest in CI, comparison + guard in CD, all CDK stacks and WSO2 per RC
Keep the last 5 PRD RCs: pipeline runs, images, artifacts
New concept for the team
main must stay releasable – we cannot leave one merged change out
To check: republishing unchanged WSO2 config is harmless; cdk deploy --all stays fast enough (incl. cross-account Felet Lambda)

g.text: ADR004 · Tag PRD releases and generate the changelog
g.textArea: How do we mark a PRD release, and how do approvers and users learn what is in it?

rect.data-content:
⭐ M1. Date tag (CalVer)
release/2026.10.20 – hotfix release/2026.10.20.1
✓ Everyone understands "the release of 20 October" ✓ Easy to automate

M2. Semantic version (nx release) – v1.4.0
✗ Needs strict commit discipline + release commit ✗ "Major" is hard to define for a UI

M3. Build id only (549747)
✗ Identifies one pipeline run, not a release

M4. No marker, pipeline history
✗ Invisible in Git, disappears with run retention

C1. CHANGELOG.md in the repo
✗ Pipeline must push to main (policy bypass) or a release PR

⭐ C2. Changelog in the pipeline, before approval
✓ Approvers see what they approve ✓ Pipeline does not write to main

⭐ C3. Release notes on the wiki, by the PO
✓ Written for people, can link ServiceNow change, tests, stories

⭐ C4. Draft from linked work items (helper for C3)
Only as good as PR ↔ work item linking

C5. A change file per PR (changesets)
✗ Friction for every PR, little gain at our size

Since 15 April 2026: 78 PRs merged, 60 (77%) follow Conventional Commits.
The biggest features do not, e.g. "Feature: Implement Automatic Summary 2.0".

g.textArea:
Proposal: M1 + C2 + C3 (C4 pre-fills the notes)
• Annotated tag release/YYYY.MM.DD[.N], placed by the pipeline after a successful PRD deployment
• Tags are never moved or deleted (pipeline has "Create tag" only, no force push)
• Changelog with nx release changelog --dry-run, shown in the CD run before ACC approval, starting from the commit PRD runs (not simply the newest tag – matters after a rollback)
• The PO writes short release notes on the wiki per PRD release (template ready)
• PR titles must follow type(#ticket): description – checked by the PR pipeline
• First tag: release/2026.09.30 on 384f0878 (what PRD runs today)

rect.data-content: PR title check = a new rule for every PR
Release notes = a new task for the PO every release
Changelog is not a file in the repo (C1 can be added later)

g.text: ADR005 · Test feature branches in a preview environment
g.textArea: Where do developers, UX and the PO try unfinished work, while TST, ACC and PRD only get main?

rect.data-content:
31 of 72 CD runs put a feature branch in TST.
A fix/ branch reached ACC; a deploy/ branch reached PRD.

E1. TST etiquette
Book TST in the channel, deploy main back afterwards
✓ Free ✗ People forget – TST still differs from main

⭐ E2. Preview environment in TST
bic-claim-assistant-web-preview + bic-claim-assistant-api-preview, deployed from any branch by a manual pipeline (same as bic-portal-preview)
✓ TST stays = main ✓ Stable address for UX and PO ✓ No Cloud Platform Team review needed

E3. New DEV environment
✓ Full isolation ✗ Needs Cloud Platform Team, AWS, secrets, WSO2 ✗ AI Brain / FELET may have no DEV

E4. Environment per PR
✗ Lots of Cloud Platform Team work, wildcard DNS + TLS ✗ Azure AD discourages wildcard redirect URIs

g.textArea:
Proposal: E2. Preview environment in TST
Together with it:
• Branch control on ACC and PRD: only main and hotfix/*
• The CD pipeline starts automatically only for main (and hotfix/*)
• TST is always main → acceptance in TST means something
• We revisit DEV or per-PR environments if one preview is not enough

rect.data-content: One branch at a time – the team agrees who uses it
Portal + BFF only: CDK and Lambda changes still share TST
Setup: preview pipeline, 2 apps in k8s-deployments, Azure AD redirect URI + API_BASE_URL

g.text: ADR006 · Handle PRD incidents with a hotfix process
g.textArea: When is something a hotfix, and how do we get a fix to PRD fast without skipping safety or losing the fix?

rect.data-content:
⭐ H1. Fix forward on main (default)
Urgent PR → new RC → promoted quickly
✓ Normal path, no merge back ✗ Releases everything else on main too

⭐ H2. Hotfix branch from the release tag (when main is not releasable)
hotfix/‹ticket› → RC → ACC → PRD → tag release/‹date›.1 → merge back the same day (Score team does this)
✓ Only the fix goes to PRD ✗ Needs merge-back discipline

H3. Cherry-pick into a release branch
✗ We have no release branches (ADR003 option D)

⭐ H4. Configuration only
Secrets via Key Vault; envVars, CPU, memory via an emergency/ branch in k8s-deployments
✓ Fastest, no build ✗ Config only, not code

🔴 Sev 1
AI Portal down or claims cannot be opened; data of the wrong claim shown; personal data exposed; actively exploitable vulnerability
→ Hotfix now. Roll back first if the last release caused it.

🟠 Sev 2
Summary or timeline not loading for many users; event ingestion stopped; critical vulnerability with exposure
→ Hotfix within the business day

⚪ Sev 3–4
Cosmetic issues, bugs with a workaround
→ Normal fix in the next release

g.textArea:
Proposal: H1 by default · H2 when main is not releasable · H4 for configuration only
Rules
• Last release < 48 h ago caused it and rollback restores service? → Roll back first (ADR007), then fix calmly
• Never skip ACC. At least 1 reviewer who is not the author
• The Engineering Team declares the hotfix and severity; the PO approves PRD
• Post in the team channel at start and end
• Postmortem within 5 working days for Sev 1 and Sev 2
• H2: open the merge-back PR to main at the start; complete it the same day with a normal merge (no squash)
• No PRD release while a hotfix PR to main is still open

rect.data-content: CI and CD must accept hotfix/* branches; branch control must allow them
Branch policy on main must allow a normal merge (no squash) for hotfix/* PRs
Until CI uses the release tag as NX base, a hotfix must be one commit
main must stay releasable for H1

g.text: ADR007 · Roll back by redeploying the previous release candidate
g.textArea: How do we go back to the previous release quickly, safely and visibly?

rect.data-content:
R1. Feature flag off
✓ Seconds, one feature only ✗ We have no flags yet (US 441556) – does not replace rollback

⭐ R2. Redeploy the previous RC
CD run for the previous RC with ROLLBACK=true
✓ Minutes, no rebuild ✓ Apps + CDK + WSO2 ✓ Visible in history

⭐ R3. Rebuild from the previous release tag (until RCs exist)
Interim
✓ Works today ✗ Slow: build + 3 environments ✗ New bits ✗ Needs quick win N5 (deployProjects)

R4. ArgoCD rollback button
✗ ArgoCD reapplies Git immediately – does not stick ✗ No audit trail

R5. Canary / blue-green (Argo Rollouts)
✓ Automatic ✗ Not installed on the Cloud Platform Team clusters – future option

g.textArea:
Proposal: R2 by default · R3 until RCs exist · never R4 · no manual k8s-deployments changes
⚡ Trigger: Sev 1 within 48 h after a release · 5xx above 2% for 10 min in Splunk · failing health or smoke checks · security exposure
👤 Decision: release captain or The Engineering Team, within 15 minutes; PO informed. Rollback stays a manual decision.
🗄 Retention: keep the last 5 PRD RCs (runs, images, CDK + WSO2 artifacts). RCs that reached ACC get a 30-day retention lease.
🔁 Rehearsal: a rollback drill in ACC every quarter.

rect.data-content: Needs release candidates first; until then R3 + quick win N5
Secrets and values.json (envVars, CPU, memory) are not part of a release – revert them separately
Artifactory / ECR lifecycle must keep at least 5 PRD versions (to confirm)
A broken event ingestion version may need an event replay (US 390288)
Replaced or deleted CDK resources cannot be restored – review the CDK diff in PRs

A fixed day every sprint
Every week

g.textArea: 2. Release window?

rect.data-content: Office hours, not on Friday afternoon
Office hours, any day

g.textArea: 3. Approvals?

rect.data-content: ACC: 1 developer · PRD: release captain + PO (or The Engineering Team)
Something else (add a sticky)

rect.data-content: 1 developer per sprint, fixed rotation, also developer on duty
Something else (add a sticky)

rect.data-content: Yes – PRD always needs someone else
No – ACC needs someone else too
